title: Vitamin B12 and folate
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It shows whether your body has enough vitamin B12 and folate.
why: For anemia, weakness, numb hands and feet, a vegetarian diet, when planning a pregnancy, or while taking certain medicines.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If you take vitamins, especially B12, folic acid, or biotin
If you are vegetarian or do not eat meat

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually fasting: no food for 8 to 12 hours. Plain water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For 24 hours, no alcohol and no hard workouts. Best not to smoke in the morning.

prepare.title: Vitamins
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor which vitamins you take. They will decide if you need a break before the test.

steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
Results usually come in 1 to 3 days. The lab will tell you when

faq.q: Should I stop vitamins before the test?
faq.a: Do not stop on your own. Tell your doctor. They will decide if a break is needed and how long.

faq.q: Why can B12 be low if I eat meat?
faq.a: Sometimes the body does not absorb it well. Your doctor will find the cause.

reminders.text: Vitamin B12 and folate test tomorrow. Do not eat after dinner. Plain water is fine.
